- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- When sentiment is negative or neutral (≤0.33), model often underestimates; adjust upward, especially if recent price is rising.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >+5% from prior day), model frequently overshoots; cap forecast at +3–5% above peak or use lagged mean.
- If sentiment turns negative mid-period, model often fails to correct downward; apply downward bias starting from day of sentiment shift.
- Mean reversion is strong in 30-day horizon; if forecast is >+10% above recent 10-day average, reduce by 1–2% per day until convergence.
- If sentiment history shows repeated “+0.67” followed by “-0.00”, model tends to overreact; dampen forecast by 1–2% on next day.
- For 30-day forecasts, if true outcome is >+10% above 18-day moving average, model often misses it; add 1–2% buffer to forecast if sentiment is bullish.
- If sentiment is mixed (e.g., alternating 0.33/0.67), model tends to oscillate; use weighted average of recent 5-day highs/lows for smoothing.
